body:
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/28909

`HivePartitioning::ApplyFiltersToFileList` copied every filter for every file, substituted the file's partition values as constants and evaluated the result with `ExpressionExecutor::TryEvaluateScalar`. That creates a new `ExpressionExecutor` per (file, filter), so functions with expensive local state rebuild it for every file - e.g. `day()`/`month()`/`year()` build a 29,584-entry `DateLookupCache` each time, making pruning ~10x slower than with `dayofmonth()`.

This PR evaluates each filter with a single executor over all files:

* The partition/filename column references of each filter are rewritten once into `BoundReferenceExpression`s into an input chunk (replacing `ConvertKnownColRefToConstants`).
* The partition/filename values of all files are loaded as (unescaped) strings into a VARCHAR `DataChunk`, one row per file, and the column references are wrapped in a cast to the partition type, so no `Value` is created per file and the cast runs as part of the filter. The filter is run with `SelectExpression` per `STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE` batch. `SelectExpression` is used rather than `ExecuteExpression` since some internal table filter functions (e.g. `__internal_tablefilter_selectivity_optional`) only have a select callback.
* Whether a filter can be evaluated on partition values only (no volatile functions, parameters, subqueries, other columns, ...) is still decided by the existing `IsScalar()`/`IsFoldable()` check, done once per filter.
* If evaluating a batch throws (e.g. a cast that fails for some partition values), the batch is split in halves recursively, so only the files for which the filter throws are kept (and the filter is preserved) while the other files are still pruned. A single bad value costs ~2*log2(2048) extra evaluations for its batch only. A partition value that cannot be cast to its `hive_types` type therefore no longer errors during pruning - the scan still raises the same `Unable to cast ... (from hive partition column ...)` error when it reads the file, unless another filter prunes that file.
* The NULL marker / unescape handling is shared with `HivePartitioning::GetValue`.
* The order of `file_filters` and of the preserved filters is unchanged.

#### Timings (10,000 hive partitions, none match, reldebug)

| filter | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `day(date) = 40` | 2.32 s | 0.22 s |
| `month(date) = 13` | 2.12 s | 0.23 s |
| `year(date) IN (1990, 1991)` | 1.24 s | 0.21 s |
| `dayofmonth(date) = 40` | 0.78 s | 0.22 s |

Added `test/sql/copy/partitioned/hive_partition_filter_evaluation.test`, covering date part pruning, mixed partition/regular column filters, volatile filters, filters that throw for some partitions, cast errors, escaped values, NULL markers and filename filters, and `hive_partition_filter_evaluation_large.test_slow`, which checks that one throwing partition value among 2100 files still prunes the rest of its batch (6/2100 files scanned).

linked_issues.body:
### What happens?

Pruning hive-partitioned files with a day() or month() filter costs up to 10x more per file than with dayofmonth().
year() is only slow for some filters. year(d) =, <, <=, > and >= are rewritten into a date range comparison, which is fast. IN, != and arithmetic are not rewritten, so they are slow..

Pruning evaluates every filter once for every file and creates a new ExpressionExecutor (HivePartitioning::ApplyFiltersToFileList calls ExpressionExecutor::TryEvaluateScalar once per file) and day/month/year speed up work by building a 29,584-entry DateLookupCache table covering 1970-01-01 to 2050-12-30.
The table lives in the executor's local state so every executor builds it from scratch (about 84μs per file for day).

I have a fix ready and I will open a PR.

| filter (10,000 files, none match, v2.0.0, median of 3) | time |
|---|---:|
| `dayofmonth(date) = 40` | 0.093 s |
| `day(date) = 40` | 0.937 s |
| `month(date) = 13` | 0.745 s |
| `year(date) = 1990` (rewritten to a date range) | 0.092 s |
| `year(date) IN (1990, 1991)`  | 0.537 s |
| `extract(day FROM date) = 40` (binds to plain function which has no table)  | 0.100 s |

Profile of the day(date) = 40 query, self time:

```
# day_query.sql: the repro's day(date) = 40 query, same lake.
perf record --call-graph dwarf --user-callchains -- duckdb < day_query.sql
perf report --no-children --sort symbol

76.23%  duckdb::Date::ExtractDay(date_t)
13.83%  duckdb::InitDateCacheLocalState<DatePart::DayOperator>
```
Both are table building (ExtractDay runs 29,584 times per file to fill it), about 90% of the time.

### To Reproduce

```sql
-- 10,000 hive partitions (date=YYYY-MM-DD/), one small file each
COPY (SELECT (DATE '2000-01-01' + i::INTEGER) AS date, i AS a FROM range(10000) t(i))
  TO 'lake' (FORMAT parquet, PARTITION_BY (date));
.timer on
-- same predicate, two spellings; both prune every file
SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet('lake/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=true) WHERE dayofmonth(date) = 40;
SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet('lake/*/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=true) WHERE day(date) = 40;
```
